text: Write a descriptive piece called The Theme Park. In your writing, focus on specific sights and
sounds to help your reader imagine the scene.
Write the opening to a story called The Witness, in which some of the people and events of a major
historical incident (real or imaginary) are seen from the viewpoint of a minor character present at
the time.
‘A set of keys, a passport, a credit card – these were all that remained on the table.’
Continue the short story (although you do not have to bring it to a conclusion). In your writing,
create a sense of character and setting.
Section B: Writing for an audience
A travel magazine invites you to write a feature called My Favourite Walk, in order to encourage
tourists to see and learn about the place where you live. Write the text of the article. In your writing,
create a sense of interest and enjoyment.
Two people with experience of working in education have been invited to contribute to a debate
on the theme Are Standards Rising or Falling? Write the text of their speeches (between 300–450
words each). In your writing, create a sense of opposing attitudes and viewpoints.
A website aimed at an older audience publishes a guide called Keeping Up to Date. It offers
readers guidance on how to use examples of modern technology (such as mobile phones and
smart televisions) and the benefits they offer. Write the text for the guide. In your writing, create a
sense of practical advice and enthusiasm.
